questions.q: What does it mean that Apex runs in 'system mode' by default?
options: Apex code can only be run by System Administrators
Apex code can read and write any record and field regardless of the running user's actual permissions, unless the developer adds enforcement
Apex automatically logs every action to a System object
System mode means Apex code can never be called by a standard user
questions.explain: System mode means Apex ignores the running user's actual sharing, CRUD, and field-level security by default, which is why developers must deliberately add enforcement where it matters.

questions.q: What do the `with sharing` / `without sharing` / `inherited sharing` keywords actually control?
options: Field-level security only
Object-level CRUD permissions only
Record-level sharing rules (role hierarchy, sharing rules, manual sharing) — nothing about CRUD or FLS
Both sharing and field-level security together, automatically
questions.explain: These keywords control only whether sharing rules are enforced for the running user; CRUD and field-level security are separate concerns enforced through different mechanisms entirely.

questions.q: Why can a class declared `with sharing` still return a field the running user's profile has no access to?
options: Because with sharing is a deprecated keyword that no longer functions
Because sharing enforcement and CRUD/field-level-security enforcement are separate mechanisms, and sharing keywords only handle the former
Because field-level security only applies to Visualforce, not Apex
Because with sharing only applies to delete operations
questions.explain: Sharing rules determine which records a user can see; field-level security is a completely separate check that with sharing does not perform on its own.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED` and `WITH USER_MODE` in a SOQL query?
options: They are identical in every respect
SECURITY_ENFORCED throws an exception if the user lacks access to a referenced field/object; USER_MODE enforces sharing, CRUD, and FLS together without throwing, silently omitting inaccessible data
USER_MODE only works in triggers, never in classes
SECURITY_ENFORCED enforces sharing rules, while USER_MODE only enforces field-level security
questions.explain: WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED throws an exception on an inaccessible field/object, while WITH USER_MODE enforces sharing, CRUD, and FLS together and simply omits what the user can't access rather than throwing.

questions.q: Why does CRUD/FLS enforcement typically matter more for an Apex REST service or an @AuraEnabled controller than for many backend trigger handlers?
options: Triggers are always exempt from all security rules by platform design
REST services and controller methods are directly invoked by a specific logged-in user, which is exactly the situation where skipping enforcement could expose data beyond that user's real permissions
AuraEnabled methods cannot be declared with sharing at all
There is no real difference; both need identical enforcement in all cases
questions.explain: A REST service or controller method acts directly on behalf of a specific end user, so skipping CRUD/FLS enforcement there risks exposing or modifying data that user's actual permissions were never meant to allow.
